messages:
joanna: Heads-up — long-running LLM service shows slow memory drift over ~12h on a dedicated node. Not seeing OOMs, but used memory climbs ~200MB every hour. Attached two profiler snapshots and a small smoketest log.

samir: thanks. can you paste the cuda memory stats from the snapshots? curious if reserved vs allocated diverge (caching allocator patterns).

joanna: sure — snippet from the nightly snapshot: 
```
Timestamp: 2026-02-17T02:12:10Z
GPU0: total=48GB, used=21.4GB
torch.cuda.memory_reserved(): 23.1GB
torch.cuda.memory_allocated(): 21.4GB
active_buffers: 42
workspace_peak: 5.6GB
```
Later (12h):
```
GPU0: total=48GB, used=23.8GB
torch.cuda.memory_reserved(): 24.4GB
torch.cuda.memory_allocated(): 23.8GB
active_buffers: 48
workspace_peak: 5.9GB
```
Looks like reserved grows a bit with allocated following. Not huge peaks but steady climb.

lee: do we have evidence of leaked CUdeviceptr handles or unfreed host pinned pages? sometimes our buffer pool retains refs due to stalled batched requests. Any stack traces from the runtime?

joanna: grabbed a profiler capture with allocations annotated to callsites. Top repeated alloc site: inference/runtime/buffer_pool.py: allocate_workspace() — call pattern: varying sequence lengths, small spikes on cold-start of long sequences.

nora: could be workspace sizing + batching heuristics keeping larger-than-needed buffers. If workspace lives in pool and we never shrink, reserved will creep. Two quick checks: 1) force pool.shrink(attempt=True) in a canary and 2) run with TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold to test fragmentation effects.

joanna: did a canary — forcing pool.release_all() every 10 min stops the drift for the test run. When we disable pool shrinks, drift resumes. So behaviour consistent with retained buffers, not an orphaned CUDA malloc leak.

samir: good signal. next: reproduce at smaller scale with a script that cycles sequence lengths and interleaves requests to hit batching edge cases. if pool.release_all() fixes it, maybe we should auto-shrink when total_reserved > X for Y minutes. But watch perf impact.

lee: also check cudnn/workspace allocations — some libs allocate persistent workspaces if configured with persistent algo. We should compare kernel selection logs on the two snapshots. If algo fallback chooses persistent, it'll hold memory.

joanna: kernel logs show stable algos; no persistent flags set. The repeated allocations map to our custom attention kernel path where we grow a temp buffer per max-seqlen.

nora: TODOs: 1) small repro script (samir) that cycles seqlen batches + intermittent flush, 2) add diagnostic hook to report "buffers_by_callsite" counts, 3) experiment with periodic shrink thresholds and measure p50/p99 latency impact.

infra-bot: deploy canary started: eng-runtime/canary/memory-shrink-2026-02-17 on node g4-11. Will collect 6h traces.

joanna: thanks — will follow the canary results. If shrink cost negligible we can add adaptive policy: auto-shrink when reserved - allocated > 2GB for > 30m.

samir: sounds good. capture NVTX around pool alloc/free in the next run so we can correlate with batching windows.

lee: also add an eval to detect regression: run 1M short inference calls to measure token latency before/after shrink. if p99 jumps, tune thresholds.

joanna: noted. sharing the two snapshots in the thread: link to s3://redwood-inference/profiles/2026-02-17/mem-drift-1 and mem-drift-2.

nora: great thread. if the canary reproduces we'll file a small runtime PR to add an opt-in adaptive shrinker behind a flag. :thumbsup:

joanna: thanks everyone — will post results from the canary here later.
